items.text: Over SSH, histgrep fails with this error because xclip is chosen whenever installed, ignoring DISPLAY.
Over SSH without X display, histgrep copies selection to local clipboard via OSC 52, not xclip.
lib/commands.sh _dotfiles_clipboard_write_cmd/copy_to_clipboard order: pbcopy → xclip -selection clipboard if DISPLAY → OSC 52.
_dotfiles_clipboard_read_cmd: pbpaste → xclip -o -sel clipboard if DISPLAY set → return empty.
scripts/tmux-copy.sh stays in scope: pbcopy → xclip if DISPLAY → tmux load-buffer -w - with buffer.
No path prints an error when no clipboard mechanism is reachable; fallback fails silently.
No wl-copy/wl-paste native Wayland support, and no OSC 52 clipboard read.
No changes to tmux mouse copy-pipe copy_to_clipboard bindings or scripts/tmux-paste.sh.
No change to histgrep itself, including its tmux send-keys branch.
xclip used only when DISPLAY is set; WAYLAND_DISPLAY alone does not qualify.
New helper _dotfiles_osc52_copy reads stdin, base64-encodes with newlines stripped (GNU/BSD portable).
In tmux: pipe to tmux load-buffer -w -; else write \e]52;c;<b64>\a to /dev/tty, target overridable; no-op if unwritable.
TDD with failing tests first in tests/clipboard.bats: write/read helper DISPLAY cases, OSC 52 writer in/out of tmux.
tests/tmux_copy.bats: xclip present, DISPLAY unset → uses tmux load-buffer -w - instead of xclip.
Quality gates must pass: just test-unit and just test.
